world.title: Canadian publisher ends novelist’s contract, halts reprints after AI traces found
world.summary: Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal ended its professional relationship with Haitian-Canadian novelist Thélyson Orélien after an independent review found traces of artificial-intelligence tags in metadata from working files for his debut novel, “It Was Either That or Die.” Boréal said it will not reprint the book
world.content: Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal ended its professional relationship with Haitian-Canadian novelist Thélyson Orélien after an independent review found traces of artificial-intelligence tags in metadata from working files for his debut novel, “It Was Either That or Die.” Boréal said it will not reprint the book or publish further work by Orélien, but could not determine how extensively AI had been used in the writing process. The publisher said it collected the novel’s drafts and commissioned an outside analysis after its effort to gather evidence with Orélien proved inconclusive. It said he later declined to provide further material. Orélien has denied that AI generated any of the book’s prose, while acknowledging that he used it for research, including historical research. He says he began writing in 2017 and completed a draft of more than 300 pages in 2019. The decision reverses Boréal’s position a week earlier, when it said it was standing by the author. The novel had already been removed from France’s Prix Goncourt shortlist after AI-detection software flagged it. Boréal said the extent of AI use may never be known. The book had been scheduled for translation in more than 20 countries.
world.image_alt: Canadian publisher ends novelist’s contract, halts reprints after AI traces found

world.title: Canada commits C$8.7 billion to shield manufacturers from U.S. tariffs
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford announced a C$8.7 billion ($6.2 billion) package on Oct. 21 to support Ontario steelmakers, automakers and critical-mineral development as U.S. tariffs hit trade. The plan includes C$5.2 billion for steel over five years and C$2.5 billion for automakers.
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford announced a C$8.7 billion ($6.2 billion) package on Oct. 21 to support Ontario steelmakers, automakers and critical-mineral development as U.S. tariffs hit trade. The plan includes C$5.2 billion for steel over five years and C$2.5 billion for automakers. Carney said tariffs have raised costs for American families and put Ontario businesses at a disadvantage. He said Canadian auto exports to the United States had fallen more than 10%, while U.S. exports to Canada had dropped more than 20%. The announcement followed the collapse of trade talks in August and President Donald Trump’s 50% tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods. Carney said he had discussed trade with Trump but reported no breakthrough, adding that Canada remains ready to negotiate. The same day, the U.S. Embassy accused Canadian politicians of trying to influence the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, citing remarks about retaliatory tariffs and a Canadian anti-tariff ad. Carney and Ford rejected the allegation. The embassy did not link the 11 Canadians it cited for illegal voting to the Canadian government.
world.image_alt: Canada commits C$8.7 billion to shield manufacturers from U.S. tariffs

world.title: North Korea readies border loudspeakers as South Korea mine dispute escalates
world.summary: North Korea will put loudspeakers for anti-South Korean propaganda on standby along the entire border within days, Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said Thursday, warning Seoul against what Pyongyang calls interference. Her announcement followed a border inspection with senior military officials and an earlie
world.content: North Korea will put loudspeakers for anti-South Korean propaganda on standby along the entire border within days, Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said Thursday, warning Seoul against what Pyongyang calls interference. Her announcement followed a border inspection with senior military officials and an earlier statement that broadcasts would resume by the end of October. The warning follows a Sept. 21 land-mine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers, two seriously. Seoul and the U.S.-led United Nations Command attributed the blast to North Korean mines; Pyongyang denies responsibility. North Korea has been adding mines, fences and anti-tank barriers as it seeks to make the border permanent. Seoul says its warning broadcasts and shots are defensive measures against North Korean troops crossing the military demarcation line. South Korea’s Defense Ministry said it would take proportionate measures if the North acts on its threats, but has not decided on a response. Seoul also said it would send a letter to the U.N. Security Council blaming North Korea for the blast, demanding an apology and urging dialogue. President Lee Jae Myung’s government halted the South’s broadcasts and dismantled fixed speakers in 2025 in an effort to reduce tensions.
world.image_alt: North Korea readies border loudspeakers as South Korea mine dispute escalates

world.title: Rubio says Musk controls Ukraine satellite access, denies White House role
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that SpaceX and its chief executive, Elon Musk, decide Ukraine’s access to the company’s satellite services, not the White House. Kyiv is seeking answers about a reported speed restriction that disrupted military drone operations. The Wall Street Journal reported that
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that SpaceX and its chief executive, Elon Musk, decide Ukraine’s access to the company’s satellite services, not the White House. Kyiv is seeking answers about a reported speed restriction that disrupted military drone operations. The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk ordered the slowdown of Starshield, a military-grade satellite service used by Ukraine; accounts differ over whether he consulted President Donald Trump and other administration officials before acting. Rubio said the administration had no advance knowledge of the change and that a private commercial contract governed access and speed limits. Trump said he was not involved, while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon had issued no directive. Ukraine’s charge d’affaires in Washington, Denys Sienik, said on Oct. 21 that speed restrictions remained in place and Kyiv had received no response from SpaceX or the Pentagon. Lawmakers from both parties have sought an investigation into the dispute, while Ukraine says the service limits have affected its defenses against Russian attacks. Rubio spoke during a trip to India and said the commercial satellite service Starlink and Starshield operate under different arrangements.
world.image_alt: Rubio says Musk controls Ukraine satellite access, denies White House role

world.title: Macron rebukes Trump over France riots as Paris bans protests
world.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday accused US President Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of exploiting France’s unrest for electoral gain after Trump blamed the violence on migrants, jihadists and communists. Macron said he saw no evidence of foreign interference in the unrest itself, but said misleadi
world.content: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday accused US President Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of exploiting France’s unrest for electoral gain after Trump blamed the violence on migrants, jihadists and communists. Macron said he saw no evidence of foreign interference in the unrest itself, but said misleading information, including AI-generated images of scenes that did not occur in France, had circulated afterward. The unrest began with student demonstrations over school conditions and grew to include protests over living costs. On Oct. 17, violence, looting and clashes with police followed mass protests in cities including Paris, Marseille and Lyon. The government acknowledged it had lost control of the violence, and more than 2,000 people were detained. Paris police banned demonstrations on Thursday in parts of the capital, including near the presidential palace, parliament, the Louvre and the Champs-Elysees. Authorities were preparing to reinforce security for protests planned for Saturday, Oct. 24, while Macron was due to meet ministers and intelligence officials for a detailed account of the unrest.
world.image_alt: Macron rebukes Trump over France riots as Paris bans protests

world.title: Greek students and teachers march over education funding, rents and living costs
world.summary: Thousands of students, teachers and public-sector workers marched in Athens and other Greek cities on Oct. 21, demanding more public funding for education, better school facilities, affordable student housing and relief from rising living costs. Police estimated about 10,000 demonstrators in Athens and its suburbs; Le
world.content: Thousands of students, teachers and public-sector workers marched in Athens and other Greek cities on Oct. 21, demanding more public funding for education, better school facilities, affordable student housing and relief from rising living costs. Police estimated about 10,000 demonstrators in Athens and its suburbs; Le Monde reported a police estimate of 20,000 across 50 cities. Protesters carried signs linking their action to student demonstrations in France and elsewhere in Europe. Participants described deteriorating school buildings, crowded classrooms and rents that make it difficult for students to stay in education. The Secondary Education Teachers’ Federation says schools need 15,000 more teachers, while rents have risen more than 115% in Athens and 93% in Thessaloniki over a decade, according to property consultancy Geoaxis. Teacher and public-sector walkouts disrupted some school and hospital services. Education Minister Sofia Zacharaki said projects worth more than €733 million are under way for student residences and facility upgrades. Student representatives have said the demonstrations will continue.
world.image_alt: Greek students and teachers march over education funding, rents and living costs

world.title: Putin agrees in principle to resume Ukraine peace talks after Nov. 10 as Kyiv urges ceasefire
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said the technical-level negotiations could take place in A
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said the technical-level negotiations could take place in Abu Dhabi and focus on a postwar security framework for Russia and Ukraine. Earlier rounds yielded little progress beyond prisoner exchanges. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv supports resuming the talks as soon as possible, preferably by early November, and proposed freezing the current front line as a first step toward a ceasefire. He also called for Ukraine to be included in decisions about its future and said Ukraine’s parliament must approve any peace settlement. Witkoff brought Putin proposals discussed a day earlier with Zelenskyy and European officials in Oslo, including security guarantees and postwar arrangements. Ushakov said the proposals contained little useful material. Moscow continues to seek terms Kyiv rejects, including Russian control of all of Donetsk and a bar on Ukrainian NATO membership. A technical-level meeting is the next step, but no firm date or venue has been announced. The Kremlin said talks could begin after Nov. 10.
world.image_alt: Putin agrees in principle to resume Ukraine peace talks after Nov. 10 as Kyiv urges ceasefire

world.title: Pope Leo needs no further cancer treatment after lung surgery
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV needs no additional cancer treatment after final tests showed that the lung adenocarcinoma removed from his right lung was localized, his doctors said Oct. 21. The 71-year-old pope underwent surgery to remove the lung’s lower lobe on Oct. 13 and left Rome’s Gemelli hospital four days later. Surgeons said t
world.content: Pope Leo XIV needs no additional cancer treatment after final tests showed that the lung adenocarcinoma removed from his right lung was localized, his doctors said Oct. 21. The 71-year-old pope underwent surgery to remove the lung’s lower lobe on Oct. 13 and left Rome’s Gemelli hospital four days later. Surgeons said the nodule was discovered by chance during routine abdominal examinations, when Leo had no symptoms. Lung cancer expert Stephen Liu said the results suggested an early-stage cancer, for which surgery can be curative. The Vatican said tests on the removed tissue confirmed the diagnosis and that specialists found no need for further treatment. Leo returned to St. Peter’s Square for his weekly audience on Oct. 21 and said he would gradually resume his duties. His planned Nov. 6-17 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru remains unconfirmed; his surgeon said he saw no medical reason to cancel, while the Vatican secretary of state said the schedule could be adjusted for recovery.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo needs no further cancer treatment after lung surgery

business.title: Anthropic reports $80.7 billion first-half loss ahead of November IPO
business.summary: Anthropic, the maker of the artificial intelligence assistant Claude, recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $13 billion a year earlier, according to a draft prospectus for its planned November initial public offering. A $72 billion accounting charge tied to the rising estimated value o
business.content: Anthropic, the maker of the artificial intelligence assistant Claude, recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $13 billion a year earlier, according to a draft prospectus for its planned November initial public offering. A $72 billion accounting charge tied to the rising estimated value of convertible bonds accounted for most of the reported loss; it did not represent cash spent operating the business. Revenue rose to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion, while computing and infrastructure spending climbed to nearly $9 billion. The prospectus also details at least $518 billion in infrastructure, computing and cloud-service commitments over a decade. Separately, Anthropic has indicated it could spend as much as $750 billion in coming years; the figures cover different scopes and should not be added together. After the disclosures, some investors discussed valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion, down from earlier expectations near $2 trillion. Anthropic told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion, up 45% from the prior quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis. Its shares are expected to begin trading in November.
business.image_alt: Anthropic reports $80.7 billion first-half loss ahead of November IPO

business.title: IBM posts 5% third-quarter revenue growth as software revenue rises
business.summary: International Business Machines, the U.S. technology company known as IBM, reported third-quarter revenue of $17.1 billion, up about 5% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $2.95 a share, topping analyst estimates. Net income rose to $2.19 billion from $1.74 billion. The results followed a weak second quarter
business.content: International Business Machines, the U.S. technology company known as IBM, reported third-quarter revenue of $17.1 billion, up about 5% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $2.95 a share, topping analyst estimates. Net income rose to $2.19 billion from $1.74 billion. The results followed a weak second quarter that IBM attributed to customers shifting IT budgets and buying scarce hardware ahead of possible price increases. Software revenue rose 8% to $7.8 billion, while infrastructure revenue increased 4% to $3.7 billion; consulting revenue was broadly flat at $5.34 billion. IBM maintained its 2026 revenue-growth forecast of 4% to 5% at constant currency and raised its free-cash-flow outlook, now expecting an increase of more than $1 billion for the year.
business.image_alt: IBM posts 5% third-quarter revenue growth as software revenue rises

business.title: Netflix co-CEO says job cuts are over for the foreseeable future
business.summary: Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters told employees at a Wednesday town hall that job cuts were over for the foreseeable future. The company had eliminated about 1,000 positions and replaced content chief Bela Bajaria with former Disney executive Peter Rice. It also dismissed film chief Dan Lin following concerns about slowing a
business.content: Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters told employees at a Wednesday town hall that job cuts were over for the foreseeable future. The company had eliminated about 1,000 positions and replaced content chief Bela Bajaria with former Disney executive Peter Rice. It also dismissed film chief Dan Lin following concerns about slowing audience engagement and growth. Netflix has spent about $20 billion a year on programming, but viewing hours rose only 2% in the first half of 2026. In the U.S., it added no net subscribers in any month during the first nine months, according to analytics firm Antenna. Netflix disputed Antenna’s methodology. Netflix’s U.S. share of television viewing was 7.8% in July, compared with YouTube’s 14.2%, Nielsen data showed. Netflix’s other co-CEO, Sarandos, said the company needs to execute better in the U.S. and cited Rice’s experience with talent relations. He said Netflix does not need a fundamental strategic shift. Rice is expected to start next week, and Netflix is planning 30 theatrical releases in 2027, including a wide release of Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” in February.
business.image_alt: Netflix co-CEO says job cuts are over for the foreseeable future

business.title: French 10-year borrowing costs top 5% as budget fears mount
business.summary: France’s 10-year government bond yield briefly exceeded 5% on Wednesday for the first time since 2002, as investors demanded higher returns amid political turmoil, street unrest and doubts over the government’s ability to rein in public debt. The yield reached 5.02% before closing at 4.99%, while the gap between it and
business.content: France’s 10-year government bond yield briefly exceeded 5% on Wednesday for the first time since 2002, as investors demanded higher returns amid political turmoil, street unrest and doubts over the government’s ability to rein in public debt. The yield reached 5.02% before closing at 4.99%, while the gap between it and Germany’s benchmark yield widened to nearly 1.6 percentage points. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s government is seeking parliamentary backing for €43 billion in proposed 2027 spending cuts. France’s debt is about 120% of gross domestic product, and the plan would still leave the deficit at 5% next year. Higher benchmark yields can also raise borrowing costs for households and companies. Moody’s is due to review France’s credit rating on Friday, Oct. 23, and parliament is scheduled to resume its budget debate on Oct. 27.
business.image_alt: French 10-year borrowing costs top 5% as budget fears mount

business.title: South Korea central bank holds rate at 3%, signals November hike
business.summary: The Bank of Korea (BOK) kept its benchmark rate at 3% on Thursday, Oct. 22, after raising it by a quarter-point in both July and August. The unanimous decision gives policymakers time to assess those increases and economic risks. The bank said the timing of future hikes would depend on inflation, growth and financial s
business.content: The Bank of Korea (BOK) kept its benchmark rate at 3% on Thursday, Oct. 22, after raising it by a quarter-point in both July and August. The unanimous decision gives policymakers time to assess those increases and economic risks. The bank said the timing of future hikes would depend on inflation, growth and financial stability. The central bank said growth this year and next is likely to exceed its August forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%, respectively, while September inflation remained at 2.9%, above its 2% target. Strong semiconductor exports and rising oil prices are among the factors shaping its outlook. Analysts expect another quarter-point increase at the next policy meeting on Nov. 26; the bank will first review third-quarter growth and October inflation data.
business.image_alt: South Korea central bank holds rate at 3%, signals November hike

business.title: Canada commits billions to steel upgrades as Hamilton layoffs loom
business.summary: U.S.-owned steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs confirmed layoffs at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant on Oct. 21 as Canada announced a C$8.7 billion ($6.2 billion) package for the steel, auto and critical-mineral industries. Hundreds of workers at Hamilton-based Stelco face imminent cuts; Cleveland-Cliffs has cited market pressures
business.content: U.S.-owned steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs confirmed layoffs at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant on Oct. 21 as Canada announced a C$8.7 billion ($6.2 billion) package for the steel, auto and critical-mineral industries. Hundreds of workers at Hamilton-based Stelco face imminent cuts; Cleveland-Cliffs has cited market pressures, including U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel. The five-year plan allocates C$5.2 billion to steelmakers and C$2.5 billion to automakers. Steel funding is intended to help mills upgrade equipment and supply Canadian and other non-U.S. markets, while auto aid is meant to accelerate the shift to electric-vehicle production. Ottawa is also putting C$1 billion toward roads to northern Ontario’s Ring of Fire mineral region, matching a previous provincial commitment.
business.image_alt: Canada commits billions to steel upgrades as Hamilton layoffs loom

business.title: GM targets two-year vehicle development and eyes-off driving by 2028
business.summary: General Motors (GM) outlined plans on Oct. 21 to use artificial intelligence to halve vehicle development time, introduce eyes-off highway driving in the Cadillac Escalade IQ in 2028 and launch a new OnStar AI assistant first in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq. The automaker says its current four- to five-year development cycl
business.content: General Motors (GM) outlined plans on Oct. 21 to use artificial intelligence to halve vehicle development time, introduce eyes-off highway driving in the Cadillac Escalade IQ in 2028 and launch a new OnStar AI assistant first in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq. The automaker says its current four- to five-year development cycle could shrink to about two years, but it did not specify when it would reach that target. The plan includes a new computing architecture for electric and gasoline vehicles, with the Escalade IQ first to receive it in 2028. GM intends to extend eyes-off driving to high-volume pickups and SUVs, though it gave no schedule for that expansion. GM plans to use lithium manganese-rich batteries and more efficient motors in its fourth-generation electric vehicles (EVs) as it seeks to compete with faster-moving Chinese automakers. GM also reported that it had taken more than $11 billion in write-downs since 2025 to adjust EV manufacturing and investment to lower-than-expected demand. Executives said the new OnStar assistant would roll out to additional models after the Lyriq. A unified OnStar phone app is planned for 2027.
business.image_alt: GM targets two-year vehicle development and eyes-off driving by 2028

business.title: UK inflation and borrowing exceed forecasts ahead of Healey’s Budget
business.summary: UK inflation accelerated as the Iran war drove fuel costs higher, while government borrowing also exceeded forecasts ahead of Finance Minister John Healey’s first Budget. Consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August and above economists’ forecast of 3.4%. The rate was the highest since Oct
business.content: UK inflation accelerated as the Iran war drove fuel costs higher, while government borrowing also exceeded forecasts ahead of Finance Minister John Healey’s first Budget. Consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August and above economists’ forecast of 3.4%. The rate was the highest since October 2025. Motor fuels were the biggest contributor to the rise: prices rose 29.8% year over year, while services inflation reached 3.7% and core inflation rose to 2.8%. Food inflation held at 1.3%. Separately, the government borrowed £24.5 billion in September, £1.8 billion more than a year earlier, and public debt topped £3 trillion. Borrowing from April to September reached £97.8 billion, £6 billion above the fiscal watchdog’s forecast. Healey will present his Budget on Oct. 28. The September inflation reading determines increases in several benefits next April. Investors expect the Bank of England to raise its benchmark interest rate from 3.75% to 4% at its Nov. 5 meeting, though no increase has yet been announced.
business.image_alt: UK inflation and borrowing exceed forecasts ahead of Healey’s Budget

science.title: Euclid space telescope discovers first comet during galaxy survey
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), after software flagged the moving object in images taken in September 2026. Ground-based astronomers confirmed the find with follow-up observations, and the International Astronomical Union’s Minor Planet Center offic
science.content: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), after software flagged the moving object in images taken in September 2026. Ground-based astronomers confirmed the find with follow-up observations, and the International Astronomical Union’s Minor Planet Center officially recognized it on Oct. 8. Euclid was designed to map distant galaxies, not search for solar system objects. Its survey images could also help identify comets for the European Space Agency’s Comet Interceptor mission, which has not yet selected a target.
science.image_alt: Euclid space telescope discovers first comet during galaxy survey

science.title: Drought-driven fires push New Guinea emissions to record levels
science.summary: Fires across New Guinea during an El Niño-driven drought have pushed estimated emissions in Papua New Guinea to nearly 32 megatons of carbon by Oct. 19, the highest total recorded by that date. Emissions on the Indonesian side exceeded 35 megatons, the third-highest total after the severe fire years of 2015 and 1997. S
science.content: Fires across New Guinea during an El Niño-driven drought have pushed estimated emissions in Papua New Guinea to nearly 32 megatons of carbon by Oct. 19, the highest total recorded by that date. Emissions on the Indonesian side exceeded 35 megatons, the third-highest total after the severe fire years of 2015 and 1997. Smoke has disrupted flights and schools and prompted advice for children and older people to wear masks; the haze has affected millions in Indonesia and spread to Singapore and Malaysia. Protests have followed, and a widow mourned her husband, a volunteer firefighter who died from smoke exposure. NASA researchers expect fires to continue until wet-season rains arrive, typically in early November in southern New Guinea.
science.image_alt: Drought-driven fires push New Guinea emissions to record levels

science.title: Study urges climate lessons to address young people
science.summary: A study of 39 young people aged 16 to 34 in Ontario found that participants often described school climate lessons as one-off units focused on individual carbon footprints. Participants also described guilt, helplessness and emotional overload. The seven online discussion groups, held in 2025, led to calls for climate
science.content: A study of 39 young people aged 16 to 34 in Ontario found that participants often described school climate lessons as one-off units focused on individual carbon footprints. Participants also described guilt, helplessness and emotional overload. The seven online discussion groups, held in 2025, led to calls for climate education that makes room for grief and community conversations rather than placing responsibility mainly on personal choices. Separate climate initiatives include Columbia Climate School's free 30-minute online webinars for learners and educators during its 2026-27 season, and Trellis' selection of 30 young professionals working on corporate climate action. Columbia requires registration and says it will post recordings online after the sessions.
science.image_alt: Study urges climate lessons to address young people

science.title: Arizona
science.summary: President Donald Trump signed legislation on Oct. 20 redesignating Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona as the country’s 64th national park, the first new national park designation since 2021. The roughly 12,000-acre site is known for volcanic rock spires and varied wildlife. The designation does not ch
science.content: President Donald Trump signed legislation on Oct. 20 redesignating Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona as the country’s 64th national park, the first new national park designation since 2021. The roughly 12,000-acre site is known for volcanic rock spires and varied wildlife. The designation does not change its boundaries or federal ownership and management. The park drew about 70,400 visitors in 2025. Supporters expect the new name to attract more visitors and bring business to nearby communities. A potential increase also raises concerns about added pressure on roads, trails, water, wildlife habitat and park staff. The National Park Service lost nearly 3,000 jobs last year and has a $24 billion deferred-maintenance backlog nationwide. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said Congress could consider additional park funding in November or December.

science.title: Stanford team revives bleached corals through brief clone contact
science.summary: Stanford researchers report that bleached coral fragments fully recovered within seven weeks in laboratory tests after brief contact with healthy, genetically identical clones, according to a study published Oct. 14 in *Science Advances*. Contact lasting five days to a week was sometimes enough; bleached fragments kept
science.content: Stanford researchers report that bleached coral fragments fully recovered within seven weeks in laboratory tests after brief contact with healthy, genetically identical clones, according to a study published Oct. 14 in *Science Advances*. Contact lasting five days to a week was sometimes enough; bleached fragments kept a few millimeters away from healthy partners died. Microscopic channels in the corals’ tissues aligned, allowing beneficial algae to move between fragments within three days. Inside bleached fragments, algae populations doubled every four days during the second week. The method requires matching clones, limiting its use across reefs. The researchers plan to test other ways to deliver algae, including collecting it from healthy corals before heat waves.
science.image_alt: Stanford team revives bleached corals through brief clone contact

science.title: Crocodile relatives tracked warm climates for 250 million years
science.summary: Crocodile relatives survived climate shifts for roughly 250 million years by following warm conditions across the globe, a study published in Science Advances found. Researchers analyzed more than 7,000 fossils, records from more than 400 extinct and living species, and climate reconstructions spanning 245 million year
science.content: Crocodile relatives survived climate shifts for roughly 250 million years by following warm conditions across the globe, a study published in Science Advances found. Researchers analyzed more than 7,000 fossils, records from more than 400 extinct and living species, and climate reconstructions spanning 245 million years. They concluded that the animals generally moved toward the poles during warmer periods and retreated toward the equator as temperatures fell. Climate models of the aftermath of the asteroid impact 66 million years ago showed that tropical and subtropical refuges remained suitable in all but the most extreme scenario tested, in which sunlight fell by 15%. The researchers said climate was not the only factor in survival: smaller body size, semiaquatic habits, flexible diets and low energy needs may also have helped. Study co-author Philip Mannion said modern crocodilians need room to move as the planet warms, while roads, farms and cities are reducing suitable habitat.
science.image_alt: Crocodile relatives tracked warm climates for 250 million years

science.title: Minnesota investigates 11-foot object suspected to be Chinese rocket debris
science.summary: Federal and state authorities in Minnesota are investigating an 11-foot-wide metal object found in a Scott Township cornfield on Oct. 14. The Stevens County Sheriff’s Office described it as a presumed space object, and it was removed from the field the following Thursday. Officials said the object poses no danger to th
science.content: Federal and state authorities in Minnesota are investigating an 11-foot-wide metal object found in a Scott Township cornfield on Oct. 14. The Stevens County Sheriff’s Office described it as a presumed space object, and it was removed from the field the following Thursday. Officials said the object poses no danger to the public. No injuries or property damage were reported. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell said the object could be part of the upper stage of China’s Zhuque-2E rocket, which re-entered over Minnesota on Sept. 15. The timing and the object’s reported diameter are consistent with that possibility. Its origin has not been confirmed. Stevens County Sheriff Jason Dingman said several agencies were helping identify it, but local authorities had received little information.
science.image_alt: Minnesota investigates 11-foot object suspected to be Chinese rocket debris

science.title: Full-scale wave test shows salt marshes can buffer coastal storms
science.summary: Researchers moved 306 square meters of intact salt marsh into the Delta Flume, a large wave-testing facility in Delft, Netherlands, and exposed it to waves as high as 2 meters. After 21 hours, the marsh surface had eroded by an average of just 7 millimeters, while its vegetation suffered progressive damage. The study f
science.content: Researchers moved 306 square meters of intact salt marsh into the Delta Flume, a large wave-testing facility in Delft, Netherlands, and exposed it to waves as high as 2 meters. After 21 hours, the marsh surface had eroded by an average of just 7 millimeters, while its vegetation suffered progressive damage. The study found that plants can reduce wave energy by more than 10%, and by as much as 50% on lower-energy coasts with waves up to 1 meter. Their effect declines as waves grow higher and vegetation is lost. Researchers say marshes could work alongside dikes and seawalls, not replace them. A Spanish coastal-engineering expert questioned how well the Dutch experiment applies to other coastlines, citing wave periods and mobile seabeds among other factors.
science.image_alt: Full-scale wave test shows salt marshes can buffer coastal storms

sports.title: NFL welcomes union review of Eagles’ care of Jalen Hurts

sports.content: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said Wednesday the league welcomes an investigation by the NFL Players Association (NFLPA), the players’ union, into how the Philadelphia Eagles handled quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clot diagnosis. The union called for a full review, saying it had been told the league did not plan to investigate. Goodell said league medical officials had reviewed the procedures and that protocols were followed. Hurts played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11 after doctors found a clot in his calf. The Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, later said he had deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs. He is taking blood thinners and cannot participate in football activities while on the medication. He is expected to miss the rest of the season.

sports.content: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta said he could leave the team when he becomes a free agent in 2027 if the sides do not agree on an extension, publicly expressing frustration with stalled negotiations. On the “Pardon My Take” podcast, he discussed the risk of playing through injury and his return this season from a season-ending back injury in 2025. LaPorta has 27 catches for 316 yards and three touchdowns in five games. The Lions and LaPorta’s representatives paused extension talks earlier this month, according to reports; LaPorta said he would remain professional on the field while his agent handles negotiations. Detroit general manager Brad Holmes has said he wants to re-sign LaPorta, and head coach Dan Campbell has publicly expressed support. Without an agreement, LaPorta could enter the open market next year.

sports.content: The NFL’s 14-game Week 7 schedule begins Thursday, Oct. 22, with the 4-2 New England Patriots visiting the 4-2 Chicago Bears. Sunday’s schedule includes Pittsburgh against New Orleans in Paris, and the Dallas Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, Oct. 26. Four teams — Buffalo, Jacksonville, the Los Angeles Chargers and Washington — are on bye. San Francisco is 6-0, while Kansas City and Minnesota are each 5-0. A Week 7 projection puts all four NFC North teams in the playoff field, which would be a first under the current playoff format, though the season is only about one-third complete. In PFF’s model, a Green Bay win at Detroit would raise the Packers’ playoff odds to 72.6%, while a loss would lower them to 38.8%.

Antetokounmpo, a two-time NBA Most Valuable Player, led Miami with 35 points and six rebounds. Edwards became the third player w
sports.content: Anthony Edwards scored 45 points as the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Miami Heat 131-106 on Wednesday in Miami, spoiling Giannis Antetokounmpo’s first regular-season game with his new team. Antetokounmpo, a two-time NBA Most Valuable Player, led Miami with 35 points and six rebounds. Edwards became the third player with multiple 40-point performances in NBA season openers, joining Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan. Minnesota’s new guard LaMelo Ball added 21 points and six assists in his Timberwolves debut. A 23-7 run spanning the end of the second quarter and the start of the third turned a one-point Minnesota lead into a 78-61 advantage. The visitors stayed in control from there. Miami coach Erik Spoelstra said the team needed to defend with more effort and disrupt opponents, while Antetokounmpo called for greater trust among teammates. Miami hosts the Detroit Pistons on Friday, and Minnesota visits the Orlando Magic that night.

Rhyne Howard added 16 points and Naz Hillmon scored 15 for Atlanta, which has won two straight after losing the series opener. Th
sports.content: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds as the Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 in Game 3 on Wednesday to take a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven WNBA Finals. Rhyne Howard added 16 points and Naz Hillmon scored 15 for Atlanta, which has won two straight after losing the series opener. The Valkyries tied the score at 49 early in the third quarter, but Atlanta answered with an 8-0 run and closed the period with a 12-2 run. The Dream have outscored Golden State 63-35 in third quarters across the series. Reese has recorded a double-double in all three Finals games, a first in WNBA history. Atlanta’s first home Finals games were moved to State Farm Arena, which seats more than 17,000, and both games there sold out. Game 4 is scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 24, in Atlanta. The Dream need two more wins for the franchise’s first championship.

sports.content: South Africa moved within six wickets of a series-leveling win after dismissing Australia for 99 and enforcing the follow-on in the second Test at Gqeberha. Australia reached 156-4 by stumps on day four, still 170 runs behind. Australia had begun the day at 3-1, but South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen took 5-33 as the visitors lost nine wickets for 96 runs. South Africa had declared at 425-9, with captain Temba Bavuma scoring 179, to establish a 326-run first-innings lead. Travis Head was unbeaten on 87 at the close, with Scott Boland 2 not out. Steve Smith, who made 28 in the first innings and passed 11,000 Test runs, remained off the field during the second innings with a neck problem. Australia coach Andrew McDonald said Smith would bat on the final day. The fifth day is scheduled for Thursday, October 22. Australia lead the three-Test series 1-0 after winning in Durban, so a South African victory would level the series before the final Test in Cape Town, starting October 27.

Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed Wednesday that the incident involved a firearm; a source told ESPN the
sports.content: The Tennessee Titans released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after an Oct. 15 practice dispute with right tackle JC Latham escalated when Elliott went to the players’ parking area to retrieve a gun from his car. Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed Wednesday that the incident involved a firearm; a source told ESPN the gun never left Elliott’s parking spot. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers intervened and helped calm Elliott, and no one was hurt. Saleh called Elliott’s actions a serious lapse in judgment but said he saw them as a possible sign that Elliott needed help. The Titans announced the release Tuesday after reviewing the incident. The NFL said it is reviewing the case under a policy that bars firearms at team facilities and other league settings. Latham said the pair had no history of bad blood. Elliott was inactive for Tennessee’s 26-20 win over Indianapolis on Sunday. The Titans, who were 1-5 before that victory, are scheduled to host the Cleveland Browns in Week 7.

sports.summary: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Tuesday’s 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona. sports.content: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Tuesday’s 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona. The club said the operation will take place in the coming days but has not given a recovery timetable. The injury is likely to keep the 25-year-old out for months and could end his season. PSG are seeking a third consecutive European title. Kvaratskhelia was named Champions League player of the season after helping the club win the trophy last season, and he has made 11 appearances for PSG this season. PSG also expect forward Ousmane Dembélé and captain Marquinhos to miss several weeks with thigh injuries sustained in the same match. Separately, Barcelona have complained to UEFA about a chainsaw-themed stadium banner. UEFA is waiting to see whether it appears in the match delegate’s report before deciding whether to act.
